- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast peak by 2–5% relative to sentiment intensity.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (sentiment < 0.3) — add 1–3% to forecast to compensate for mean reversion bias.
- Avoid overreacting to recent spikes — cap forecast overshoot at +3% above 14-day moving average unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- When sentiment shifts from bearish to bullish mid-horizon, adjust forecast downward for 3–5 days before reversing upward.
- For 30-day forecasts, apply a 1–2% downward bias if sentiment history shows high volatility or mixed sentiment (0.3–0.7 range).
- If sentiment is consistently high (>0.7) over last 5 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- Correct for lag: if true outcome is >10% above forecast at day 10–15, reduce forecast by 0.5–1% per day until convergence.
